proposed.explanation:
You asked whether Edita's 2025 net profit grew by more than 50 % versus 2024, and you set that as the trigger for buying more. I cannot confirm that trigger. The FY 2025 consolidated net-profit figure (printed as 2,695,301,670 EGP) is marked AMBIGUOUS in the source document because a stamp covers the cell on the scanned page. Per protocol I must not use an AMBIGUOUS figure in any calculation, so the year-on-year growth rate is indeterminate and your 50 % condition is neither met nor refuted on the evidence available.

What the verified data does show is directionally positive: consolidated revenue rose from 16,146,545,699 EGP (2024) to 20,915,072,432 EGP (2025), and basic/diluted EPS doubled from 1.09 EGP to 2.18 EGP. These are consistent with a strong profit increase, but EPS is not a substitute for the net-profit line you asked about, and revenue growth does not guarantee a 50 %+ profit growth.

Because the buy trigger cannot be confirmed, no additional purchase is made. There is likewise no verified evidence of deterioration that would justify selling. The appropriate action is to hold your existing 1,000 EFID shares.

Two important caveats for your 3-year, medium-risk profile: (1) your portfolio is currently 100 % concentrated in a single equity; adding more EFID would deepen that concentration, which the suitability analyst flags as a structural mismatch with your medium loss tolerance. (2) Before you act on the 50 % trigger in the future, obtain a clean, un-stamped copy of the FY 2025 consolidated income statement (or the audited filing on the EGX website) so the 2025 net-profit figure can be verified. Until then, the condition remains open.

This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns. The AMBIGUOUS figure means the true 2025 profit could be higher or lower than the printed number; all conclusions about growth are therefore provisional.

reports.investor:
## Suitability & Portfolio Assessment

### On your specific question – Edita's 2025 net-profit growth

I can only flag a **data-integrity problem** here; I will not interpret the company's financials for you.

| Period | Printed figure (EGP) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| FY 2024 (31 Dec 2024) | 1,606,727,698 | **Verified** |
| FY 2025 (31 Dec 2025) | 2,695,301,670 | **Ambiguous** – the 2025 cell is covered by a stamp on the scanned page and cannot be read with confidence |

Because the 2025 figure is unreadable, I **cannot confirm** the growth rate. If the printed number were correct, the arithmetic would give roughly **+67.7 %**, which would clear your 50 % threshold. But that number is not verified, so the condition you set ("I will buy more if it grew by more than 50 %") **cannot be treated as met** on the evidence available. You would need a clean, un-stamped copy of the FY 2025 consolidated statement (or the audited filing on the EGX website) before acting on that trigger.

---

### What the portfolio allows right now

| Item | Amount (EGP) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Free cash | **10,000** | Immediately deployable |
| EFID shares (1,000 × 20.40) | **20,400** | Sellable on the open market; would free up cash but crystallise a gain/loss |
| **Total investable assets** | **30,400** | |

So the maximum you could commit *without* selling anything is the **10,000 EGP cash**. Selling any of the 1,000 EFID shares would add to that, but it would also reduce your existing position.

---

### Suitability snapshot

| Factor | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Horizon (3 yr)** | Short-to-medium. Enough for a growth tilt, but not long enough to ride out a deep single-stock drawdown comfortably. |
| **Liquidity needs** | Low – you keep a separate emergency fund, so the 10,000 EGP cash and the shares are genuinely investable. |
| **Loss willingness – medium** | You are comfortable with moderate drawdowns but not with a 40-50 %+ hit to a large slice of your portfolio. |
| **Loss capacity – medium** | A 50 % loss on the full 30,400 EGP portfolio (≈ 15,200 EGP) would be painful but survivable; a 50 % loss on a *concentrated* position would be harder to absorb. |
| **Current concentration** | **100 % in a single equity (EFID).** This is the dominant risk in the portfolio. Adding more EFID would push concentration even higher, which sits uncomfortably with a *medium* loss tolerance and a 3-year horizon. |

---

### Key suitability observations (no action recommended)

1. **Concentration is the binding constraint.** With every dinar already in EFID, any additional purchase deepens a single-name bet. For a medium-loss-tolerance investor on a 3-year horizon, that is a structural mismatch regardless of how strong the latest earnings print looks.

2. **The 10,000 EGP cash is the only "free" capital.** Committing all of it to the same stock would leave zero diversification buffer. A portion (or all) could alternatively be directed toward a different asset class or held as dry powder, which would better match a medium risk profile.

3. **The 3-year horizon is workable but not generous** for a single-stock growth position. If the thesis on EFID weakens, you have limited time to reposition without locking in a loss.

4. **Your 50 %-growth trigger is currently unverifiable.** Before any additional commitment, the FY 2025 net-profit figure needs to be confirmed from a clean source. Until then, the condition you set for yourself is not satisfied.

I have not recommended a buy, sell, or hold. The points above are the suitability parameters the team should weigh before any allocation decision is made.
